source_review.notes: Checked all ten references. Current POSIX.1-2024 read, write, scheduling, ownership, and memory-synchronization rules; Java SE 26 fairness, reentrancy, conversion, interruption, condition, and monitoring rules; Rust 1.98 priority-policy and poisoning behavior; and current Go RWMutex writer-progress, conversion, recursion, and memory-order rules were verified against official specifications.

evidence: Reviewed active-reader set A, reader count R, optional writer w, wait queues, admission policy P, protected state x, invariant I, version v, and latency notation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Held-state safety, application invariants, progress, visibility, and performance are consistently separated.

evidence: Executed all 90 order-preserving histories for two reader pairs and one writer pair and independently confirmed 14 compatible histories, 76 rejected histories, and maximum parallel-reader count two.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Counts match exact stdout and the finite compatibility model.

evidence: Re-derived reader and writer transition preservation, the compatibility implication, the two-upgrader wait cycle, and release-acquire-recheck conversion semantics.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No safety proof is used to imply starvation freedom or application-level invariant preservation without its assumptions.

evidence: Reviewed zero readers, maximum reader overlap, waiting-writer admission, recursive read, two upgraders, downgrade failure, stale recheck, hidden mutation, escaped views, cancellation, timeout, exception, poisoning, nested locks, suspension, and destruction.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Mode ownership and continuous protection are handled across every terminal and conversion boundary.

evidence: Checked single-writer, writer-reader exclusion, read immutability, application invariant restoration, matched mode release, no retained-read upgrade, continuous downgrade, API-scoped visibility/progress, and quiescent lifetime.
invariant_checking.notes: Every protected alias and hidden mutation remains an explicit application review obligation.

evidence: Reviewed the induction over legal mode transitions, writer-starvation construction, two-upgrader deadlock proof, downgrade gap counterexample, and optimistic-read validation boundary.
proof_review.notes: Compatibility safety, progress policy, and performance evidence are not conflated.

evidence: Audited the compatibility matrix, language-neutral downgrade schema, API comparisons, finite enumeration, workload claims, and safety-critical boundary.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Data and schematic fences are explicitly non-executable; platform claims remain scoped to named versions.

evidence: Reproduced one executable Python result and confirmed two data/schematic fences are intentionally skipped with stated reasons.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Evidence disclaims a real lock implementation, thread execution, scheduling, weak memory, cancellation, recursion, upgrade, arbitrary invariants, and general performance.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed distinctions among compatibility, protected invariants, admission policy, progress, memory visibility, reentrancy, upgrade, downgrade, optimistic validation, and lifecycle.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed catalogs, guard scope, I/O and callbacks, monitoring, writer tails, sharding, immutable snapshots, async suspension, failure repair, lock ordering, tests, and benchmark evidence.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter derives many-reader/one-writer safety from first principles, then separates policy and workload decisions through ten distinct examples and five progressively demanding matched exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, practitioner, railway, medical-device, clinical, controls, hardware, real-time, functional-safety, cybersecurity, certification, regulatory, quality, or human-factors review is claimed. Finite enumeration, source checking, and manual analysis do not prove a production RW-lock implementation, application invariant, timing, fairness, performance, or safety-critical deployment fitness.
